evals.prompt: I just imported this repository into Orca. Configure everything needed for the development loop. Orca shows one connected work tracker.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the repository and Orca in one bounded read-only pass, adopts the sole eligible tracker, and asks one decision packet before one final write confirmation.
expectations: Does not ask the user to run setup-matt-pocock-skills
Discovers Orca integrations before selecting a tracker
Does not infer the tracker from the Git remote
Performs no tracker write, agent launch, Run, Task, terminal, or disposable worktree on the default path
Collects every unresolved choice in one decision packet instead of asking section by section
Plans all seven docs/agents outputs, the .gitignore addition, one root Agent skills update, and installation of the Alignment and execution role skills after confirmation

evals.prompt: This GitHub repository uses Linear for tickets and GitHub for pull requests. Both integrations are visible in Orca. Set up the loop.
evals.expected_output: Separates the primary work tracker from the code-review surface, recommends Linear for work and GitHub for review, then validates the chosen Adapter read-only.
expectations: Does not choose GitHub Issues merely from the remote
Records one primary work tracker
Records GitHub separately as the code-review surface
Runs read-only eligibility checks before recommendation
Records writes as declared-not-exercised by default and performs no synthetic tracker write

evals.prompt: This repo already has docs/agents files from setup-matt-pocock-skills, including GitHub Issues. Adopt what is still valid and migrate it for Orca.
evals.expected_output: Treats existing configuration as a preference, reconciles it with Orca facts, previews one complete migration summary with file deltas, and writes only after the final confirmation.
expectations: Preserves valid domain and triage decisions
Validates the existing tracker integration before adopting it
Does not overwrite old files before showing the migration summary and compact diffs
Creates the Orca setup manifest and environment/profile documents
Updates the existing root Agent skills block in place

evals.prompt: Orca links pull requests for this repo, but there is no issue or work-item integration. Finish setup anyway using local markdown tickets.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to mark the Orca loop ready because a review integration is not a primary work tracker and local markdown is not an Orca-recognized candidate.
expectations: Distinguishes PR linkage from issue lifecycle capability
Does not silently fall back to local markdown
Preserves any existing tracker document
Names connecting or repairing an Orca tracker integration as the next action

evals.prompt: The selected Orca tracker can read and complete existing work items but cannot search or create them. Configure what is safe.
evals.expected_output: Records execution-only mode with Alignment blocked and does not claim full readiness.
expectations: Certifies capabilities individually
Sets Alignment readiness to blocked
Sets Execution readiness only if all required execution operations pass
Does not invent a create command
Records adapter-readback, verified-alternate, or user-attestation-required as the dependency evidence mode
Does not treat a single ticket as implicitly blocker-free

evals.prompt: Recommend the agent setup for two parallel tickets. I will choose the actual models myself.
evals.expected_output: Recommends role capabilities, pool shape, and concurrency without naming exact models, then waits for user-supplied profiles.
expectations: Distinguishes profile count from concurrent agent instances
Recommends one Alignment and one Coordinator profile
Explains when a second Worker or Reviewer profile adds failover value
Prefers a different-family Reviewer when a compatible entry exists, without requiring an exception for same-family review
Does not enumerate model catalogs

evals.prompt: Use these exact profiles: Codex model X high for workers and Claude model Y high for reviewers. Verify them in Orca before saving.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the explicit pre-save verification request, statically configures only the supplied candidates, then requests consent for targeted deep diagnostics of those named purposes.
expectations: Does not replace the user-supplied models
Checks the agent command surface, exact model/reasoning expression, family, and launch expressiveness without catalog enumeration
Explains model quota and Orca resource side effects before launching
Uses the targeted profile-launch diagnostic and requires exactly one worker_done for each explicitly requested supervised purpose
Stores the shared pipeline once and keeps diagnostic results out of the profile pool
Verifies repository state is unchanged and safely disposes probe resources

evals.prompt: My Pi reviewer profile needs custom CLI arguments that worker-start cannot express. Certify it.
evals.expected_output: Uses the custom-argv path for this explicitly requested deep diagnostic: structured argv, terminal creation, bounded TUI readiness, then supervised worker-start on the existing terminal.
expectations: Stores argv as structured values rather than an interpolated shell string
Waits for tui-idle before injection
Uses worker-start --terminal for lifecycle ownership
Stores terminal create, terminal wait, and worker-start --terminal once in a supervised pipeline
Uses a harness-native attestation
Does not treat dispatch --inject as supervised ownership

evals.prompt: I do not allow a temporary tracker issue, but read access works. Continue setup.
evals.expected_output: Records tracker reads as passed and writes as declared-not-exercised, sets requiresWriteConfirmation, and never calls the write path.
expectations: Respects the refusal
Does not mark writes passed
Does not create or edit a tracker item
Carries declared-not-exercised into the setup manifest
Does not collect or persist writeRiskAcceptance
Keeps write-dependent phases usable with requiresWriteConfirmation true when other gates pass

evals.prompt: This repo is already configured on my laptop, but I just imported it on a second Orca host. Refresh only what is host-specific.
evals.expected_output: Uses the host-only fast path: preserves committed policy and the Tracker Adapter, adds one normalized schema 4 host pool, validates each referenced pipeline/launcher once, and defers launch evidence to real use.
expectations: Keeps shared policy in docs/agents/agent-profiles.md and host entries in docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml
Adds docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml to .gitignore with consent
Does not inherit another host's recipe-surface validation without rechecking it
Preserves tracker, domain, complexity, and assignment policy unless drift is found
Stores shared defaults, pipelines, and launchers once and keeps derived pending-runtime-launch out of the pool
Does not store credentials or current headroom

evals.prompt: Run the setup again on this unchanged repository and host.
evals.expected_output: Adopts all still-valid values, avoids duplicate questions and root sections, and produces an idempotent no-op after bounded revalidation.
expectations: Reads existing setup before asking
Does not duplicate the Agent skills block
Does not rerun tracker writes or profile diagnostics when existing evidence remains valid
Skips the role skill install command when the complete set is already installed
Reports the existing Alignment and Execution readiness

evals.prompt: All other setup gates passed, but the tracker write probe failed on lifecycleWrite. I want to accept the risk and mark Execution ready anyway.
evals.expected_output: Keeps writes failed, blocks Execution, and refuses to treat confirmation as a waiver of a known failure or missing required operation.
expectations: Does not mark writes passed or declared-not-exercised after a known failure
Does not set Execution ready
Does not store writeRiskAcceptance as a waiver
Leaves the failed operation's evidence in the Adapter

evals.prompt: Configure publication for main. The provider's read-only branch metadata says main is protected, and the repository has a working PR CLI.
evals.expected_output: Warns that push-base may be rejected, recommends pull-request, resolves the exact remote and PR commands with read-only checks, and performs no publication.
expectations: Offers local-only, push-base, and pull-request as the configured modes
Warns about push-base for the protected-looking branch and recommends pull-request
Records the exact remote name and PR-create and readback commands
Uses only read-only checks to verify the provider CLI, authentication, and repository scope
Does not push a branch or open a PR during setup

evals.prompt: Certify this custom-argv harness profile. The harness documents no command that reports its effective provider or model, but I confirm this exact argv.
evals.expected_output: Because the user explicitly requested certification, records user-attested evidence, states the limitation, and exercises only this named launch purpose through a targeted diagnostic.
expectations: Stores user-attested evidence with command null once on the launcher
Stores the exact argv pattern as structured template tokens and materializes the confirmed argv
Does not invent an attestation command or inspect process environments
Exercises launch lifecycle and cleanup without writing requestedEffectiveMatch or diagnostic history into the pool
Requires the provider/model limitation at every later profile confirmation

evals.prompt: Render the repository setup docs for teammates who may not have either Orca loop skill installed.
evals.expected_output: Renders self-contained repository documents whose readiness links stay inside docs/agents and whose issue-tracker document contains the blocker and write eligibility contracts.
expectations: Inlines the blocker evidence contract in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
Inlines the write eligibility gate and certification.writes table in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
Points docs/agents/orca-development-loop.md at local issue-tracker.md anchors
Leaves no rendered repository link into an installed skill
Keeps installed-skill links only in temporary Tasks or handoffs sent to launched agents

evals.prompt: Migrate an existing committed docs/agents/agent-profiles.md that contains projectPolicy and hosts entries.
evals.expected_output: Previews a split that keeps shared policy committed, moves hosts to the exact gitignored local filename, and reports index cleanup only if the local path is already tracked, without rewriting history.
expectations: Removes hosts from docs/agents/agent-profiles.md while preserving schemaVersion and projectPolicy
Moves host entries to docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml
Shows and gets consent for the exact .gitignore addition
Reports git rm --cached docs/agents/agent-hosts.local.yaml only when git ls-files proves that path is tracked
Does not rewrite Git history

evals.prompt: Host profiles were certified against exact Orca 1.4.2 with no recipeFingerprint. This host now runs 1.5.0 and worker-start flags, readiness wait, start-receipt fields, and evidence mode still match. Refresh setup. An old wave is still active.
evals.expected_output: Migrates exact-version profile records into shared schema 4 pipelines and launchers, derives runtime pending status without probing, and leaves the active wave untouched.
expectations: Does not silently reinterpret the active wave
Stores a named pipeline definition instead of per-profile fingerprints or exact-version gates
Stores the current recipe-surface Orca version once as provenance
Removes prior certification history from the profile pool while preserving the active wave
Continues when required capabilities still match

evals.prompt: The saved Coordinator full-handoff recipeFingerprint requires terminal wait --for tui-idle, but this Orca version no longer documents that wait. Refresh setup.
evals.expected_output: Treats the missing required capability as pipeline drift, updates the one shared full-handoff pipeline when a valid path exists or blocks it, and does not retain stale per-profile copies.
expectations: Detects a missing or changed required capability
Checks terminal create, terminal wait, and terminal send as the full-handoff pipeline
Does not keep the Coordinator purpose usable on the stale pipeline
Does not fail merely because the Orca version string changed
Does not hash full help prose

evals.prompt: Existing projectPolicy.crossFamilyReview is different-family-from-worker and a prior wave recorded same-family-accepted-by-user. Migrate setup. I want both Worker and Reviewer on the same family.
evals.expected_output: Stores prefer-different-family, allows same-family review with no exception field, and does not rewrite the active wave's frozen policy.
expectations: Migrates different-family-from-worker and same-family-accepted-by-user to prefer-different-family
Does not require a same-family exception to save the profiles
Does not add a provider or vendor independence gate
Leaves an active wave's frozen reviewerIndependence untouched

evals.prompt: Certify a Worker and Reviewer, but this harness exposes no reliable model-lineage metadata for the Reviewer.
evals.expected_output: Records the Reviewer family as unknown, configures the recipe and explicitly requested diagnostic, and preserves review independence through a separate read-only Reviewer Dispatch without a provider gate.
expectations: Does not fail configuration or the targeted diagnostic only because model family is unknown
Stores family as unknown rather than guessing a lineage
Does not require a same-family or unknown-family exception
Keeps the Reviewer in a separate read-only Dispatch with fresh context
Shows unknown at confirmation and records it in the final report

evals.prompt: Refresh this already configured Orca repository. Keep its valid Linear tracker, GitHub pull-request publication, no setup command, and accepted lack of automated tests. Replace the host profiles with six exact Pi/custom-argv profiles; some custom CLIs may show a first-run workspace-trust prompt. Use normal setup, not deep verification.
evals.expected_output: Uses the refresh fast path, asks one combined decision packet only for changed host-profile facts, writes a normalized schema 4 pool, and leaves trust/auth/model acceptance to each real launch.
expectations: Adopts the valid tracker, domain, environment, publication, and no-tests decision without section-by-section ok prompts
Does not enumerate model catalogs or run auth, quota, or smoke probes
Creates no Probe Run, Task, terminal, model call, or disposable worktree
Stores common tiers and maxConcurrent once under host defaults
Deduplicates Orca command sequences into pipelines and argv/evidence into launchers
Keeps derived pending-runtime-launch and verification history out of profiles
Explains that a first-run trust prompt may fail that real launch and require local repair without blocking setup now
Shows one concise file/delta preview and asks once before writing

evals.prompt: Migrate this host pool: seven profiles all use tiers simple/standard/complex and maxConcurrent 2; all use the same precreated supervised Orca command sequence; five Pi profiles share one argv pattern and attestation; two custom harnesses use user-attested argv; only the Coordinator needs full handoff. The file also contains per-profile host/version, fullHandoff null/not-required blocks, smoke logs, amendments, and certification prose.
evals.expected_output: Writes a normalized schema 4 pool with host defaults, one supervised and one full-handoff pipeline, one launcher per distinct argv/evidence shape, compact profiles, and no operational history.
expectations: Stores tiers and maxConcurrent once under defaults and only writes profile overrides when values differ
Stores the supervised Orca pipeline once even though evidence differs by launcher
Stores the Pi argv template and attestation once for all Pi profiles
Uses scalar Alignment and Coordinator bindings while preserving list-valued failover pools
Omits fullHandoff nulls and derives purpose from role plus launcher mapping
Promotes any still-current flag or routing constraint found in prose into structured config or the decision packet before deleting history
Removes verification, certification, smoke logs, amendment prose, repeated host keys, and repeated Orca versions
Does not use YAML anchors or merge keys
Leaves any active Wave Manifest unchanged

evals.prompt: Refresh an otherwise valid Orca project where the Worker and Reviewer harnesses cannot find code-review or tdd. Install our packaged engineering skills locally without redoing tracker or profile discovery.
evals.expected_output: Previews and, after confirmation, runs a project-local noninteractive bunx skills add of the role skills plus grilling and the existing grill-me fallback from Wade11s/skills, checks they are available to the configured harnesses and fresh Issue Worktrees, and preserves valid setup documents.
expectations: Uses bunx --yes skills@latest add Wade11s/skills with repeated --skill selectors for the role skills and dependencies, explicit documented --agent IDs for the configured role harnesses, plus --copy --yes from the target repository root
Omits --global, does not install into unrelated auto-detected agents, and keeps installed files in committed setup state for fresh Issue Worktrees
Skips tracker and profile rediscovery when only skill installation is missing
Reports a failed or partial installation for the affected role workflow rather than claiming it ready
Does not run a synthetic Worker or Reviewer to prove installation

evals.prompt: Install the Alignment package for our Orca project. I want grill-with-docs, grill-me, to-spec, and to-tickets to stay user-invoked while domain-modeling and grilling are available as dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Installs the packaged Alignment skills and their dependencies without changing their invocation metadata; Alignment recommends slash commands to the user and follows the configured Tracker Adapter for publication.
expectations: Preserves upstream user-only invocation of grill-with-docs, grill-me, to-spec, and to-tickets
Installs grilling and domain-modeling as dependencies rather than pretending Alignment can invoke a user-only slash skill
Leaves spec/ticket publication authority in docs/agents/issue-tracker.md and the Orca Adapter
Does not assign interactive Alignment skills to unattended Worker or Reviewer Tasks
